title: [Mouse Jump] - Settings preview thumbnail too small

judgment.rationale: The current Mouse Jump preview path still hard-codes a 283px settings-card content height, while the reporter has now posted a WIP screenshot showing the corrected layout from an external public fix. No upstream PowerToys PR covers it yet, so the issue remains an actionable design rather than an existing fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design that sizes the preview from the available settings-card bounds instead of a fixed 283px image region.

evidence.fact: The issue reports a Mouse Jump settings preview clipped after the WinUI migration.
The current preview path uses hard-coded settings-card/content dimensions when rendering the bitmap.
The external public PR explicitly says its optional maximum-size LayoutHelper change fixes PowerToys issue 50436.
The latest comment shows a corrected thumbnail and the timeline cross-references mikeclayton/FancyMouse#96 as the public implementation precedent.

fix_assessment.rationale: A public implementation precedent exists, but it is not an upstream PowerToys change and must be integrated and verified in the current settings UI.

proposed_fixes.title: Constrain Mouse Jump preview layout to available card size
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The preview generator uses hard-coded dimensions instead of the actual maximum space available in the WinUI settings card.
plan: Add an optional maximum-size input to the preview layout calculation.
Pass the rendered settings-card bounds from the Mouse Jump view model/panel.
Scale or arrange the preview within those bounds while preserving its aspect ratio.
verification: The reported clipped preview is fully visible at the original reproduction size.
Narrow and enlarged settings cards both render without cropping.
A resize or theme change does not regress preview layout.

confidence.rationale: The public related PR identifies the same layout change and explicitly references this PowerToys issue.

issue_context.summary: The Mouse Jump settings preview is clipped after the WinUI migration because the preview layout is generated with fixed dimensions.
known_information: The issue is a UI regression associated with the v0.101 migration.
MouseUtilsViewModel_MouseJump uses fixed settings-card and content heights for preview generation.
FancyMouse PR #96 publicly describes the matching maximum-size fix.
The latest public comment shows a corrected thumbnail and indicates the reporter is already prototyping the fix externally.
inferences: The fixed preview dimensions can exceed the available settings card and crop the rendered bitmap.
Passing an available maximum size through the layout helper should preserve the preview within the card.
issue_context.analysis: This is a code-local layout regression, not a diagnostic or ownership problem. The next maintainer decision is whether to approve the bounded layout fix and port the public precedent into PowerToys.

actions.label: Approve Mouse Jump preview sizing design
actions.note: Localized settings-preview fix; no upstream action is taken automatically.
